question: What is the medical term for the point of contact between bones?
explanation: An articulation is the anatomical meeting point where two or more bones connect in the skeletal system. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T7#GNS121_U3_T7_h1)

question: Why does a skull suture have a different structure than a shoulder joint?

options.A: Skull sutures prioritize protection over movement
options.B: Shoulder joints require rigid fixation for posture
options.C: Skull bones need continuous friction reduction
options.D: Shoulder joints lack cartilage for stability

explanation: Different joints are built for specific tasks, balancing the need for movement against the need for structural protection. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T7#GNS121_U3_T7_h1)

question: A freely movable joint is functionally classified by what name?
explanation: Diarthrosis is the functional term designated for joints that allow a wide range of free movement. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T7#GNS121_U3_T7_h2)

question: A patient with a rigid cranial suture has which functional type of joint?
explanation: Synarthrosis describes joints that do not permit any movement, keeping the connected bones completely fixed. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T7#GNS121_U3_T7_h2)

question: What mechanical role do joints play when skeletal muscles contract?
explanation: Joints serve as the pivot points or fulcrums that allow bones to swing when muscles apply pulling force. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T7#GNS121_U3_T7_h3)

question: Which joint type allows multiaxial movement in multiple directions?
explanation: Ball-and-socket joints feature a rounded head fitting into a cuplike cavity, enabling movement across multiple planes. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T7#GNS121_U3_T7_h3)

question: Which structures provide the primary tensile strength holding weight-bearing joints together?
explanation: Ligaments are strong bands of fibrous connective tissue that connect bone to bone, preventing excessive or abnormal joint movement. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T7#GNS121_U3_T7_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of lower extremity joint stability during walking?

options.A: Absorbing and distributing compressive body forces
options.B: Producing red blood cells for the limbs
options.C: Eliminating friction inside the joint capsule
options.D: Increasing the speed of muscle contraction

explanation: Weight-bearing joints must manage heavy downward loads safely without buckling or injuring the surrounding tissue. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T7#GNS121_U3_T7_h4)

question: Which substance lubricates synovial joints and nourishes articular cartilage?
explanation: Synovial fluid fills the joint cavity to reduce friction and supply nutrients to cartilage, which lacks its own blood supply. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T7#GNS121_U3_T7_h5)

question: Why is articular cartilage vulnerable to permanent damage once injured?

options.A: It continuously secretes destructive inflammatory enzymes
options.B: It lacks a direct blood supply for healing
options.C: It contains high concentrations of pain receptors
options.D: It relies entirely on bone marrow for oxygen

explanation: Because articular cartilage is avascular, it cannot easily repair itself when torn or worn down. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T7#GNS121_U3_T7_h5)

question: What sensory receptors in joints inform the brain about body position?
explanation: Proprioceptors detect the physical state and position of joints and muscles, relaying crucial data to the central nervous system. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T7#GNS121_U3_T7_h6)

question: How do joints help a person maintain an upright posture against gravity?

options.A: By locking all spinal vertebrae into rigid, immovable positions
options.B: By storing excess calcium to increase skeletal weight
options.C: By allowing micro-adjustments in skeletal alignment through sensory feedback
options.D: By generating continuous heat to keep supporting muscles relaxed

explanation: Constant sensory input from joints enables the body to make subtle, continuous posture corrections. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T7#GNS121_U3_T7_h6)

question: Which condition is primarily characterized by autoimmune inflammation of the synovial membrane?
explanation: Rheumatoid arthritis is a systemic autoimmune disease where the immune system attacks the joint's synovial lining. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T7#GNS121_U3_T7_h7)

question: A patient exhibits bone-on-bone friction due to loss of articular cartilage. Which condition is present?
explanation: Osteoarthritis is a degenerative joint disease caused by the mechanical breakdown of articular cartilage over time. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T7#GNS121_U3_T7_h7)
